subject: Network boundary narrative and isolated-path evidence for Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: isolation narrative + deployment trace for Dedicated/Private

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Acme's audit team has asked us to provide an explicit narrative and evidence that shows how Redwood enforces network and control-plane isolation between Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want:

- an annotated network diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane boundaries, and typical egress paths
- a short narrative tying those diagram elements to SIG/CAIQ control IDs (especially network segregation and multi-tenant isolation)
- a short deployment trace (example request flow) demonstrating enforced isolation across a Dedicated pool vs a Private VPC install

Can you send a one-page narrative and the diagrams we can hand to the auditors by EOD? If you have a mapping to CAIQ/SIG controls that would save a follow-up.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp
Attachment: none
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: isolation narrative + deployment trace for Dedicated/Private

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We're putting together a concise package. High level: we will provide an annotated SVG of the boundary diagram, a CSV matrix that shows control-plane egress/ingress allowances per deployment mode, a short narrative (one page) mapping to SIG/CAIQ, and a deployment trace file with actual request hops (redacted).

Karthik & Soojin: tagging you for review — can you confirm the control IDs and a single trace example we can share? I drafted the narrative below (internal) and I attached the diagram stub.

-- Draft narrative (internal):
Redwood enforces isolation between Dedicated and Private deployments using layered boundaries: compute tenancy (dedicated GPU pools vs tenant VMs in customer VPC), control-plane tenancy (shared control plane with tenant-scoped control-plane tokens vs private control plane for on-prem/VPC), network zoning (isolated subnets and egress gateways per deployment class), and enforced egress policies with least-privilege NAT/Bastion routes. Controls are instrumented with audit logs and token-scoped RBAC. See attached: redwood_isolation_annotated.svg (diagram), controlplane-egress-matrix.csv (matrix), deployment-trace-20260708.txt (example trace).

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_isolation_annotated.svg (diagram stub)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: isolation narrative + deployment trace for Dedicated/Private

Adding detail for the mapping to SIG/CAIQ.

Jonas — good draft. A few concrete notes to include in the one-pager and mapping doc:

1) Control-plane separation: for Private (VPC or on-prem) customers we offer an optional private control plane (customer-managed endpoint) — map to SIG: NET-SEG-4 and CAIQ: NET-3. This reduces cross-tenant control-plane metadata exposure.
2) Data-path tenancy: Dedicated uses physically reserved GPU pools and subnet-scoped workers; map to SIG: TEN-01 and CAIQ: TEN-2.
3) Egress policing: we enforce egress allowlists per-customer with network address translation at dedicated gateways; map to SIG: NET-EP-2 and CAIQ: NET-5.
4) KV/Cache isolation: per-tenant KV namespaces and per-request token-scoped cache keys — map to SIG: DATA-ISOL-3.

I redlined the diagram and added a quick CSV showing which egress ports/protocols are allowed for each deployment mode. Also added a small trace (deployment-trace-20260708.txt) showing a sample request flow for a Dedicated request that falls back to an isolated cache tier.

Sooj: can you sanity-check the wording about audit logs and token scoping? If ok, I'll produce a compact CAIQ mapping PDF.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: controlplane-egress-matrix.csv, deployment-trace-20260708.txt

Hi Alice — sharing the package for your auditors. Attached:
- redwood_isolation_annotated.svg — diagram with control-plane and data-plane boundaries annotated and example tenant overlay
- controlplane-egress-matrix.csv — per-deployment egress/ingress matrix (ports, protocols, justification)
- caiq-mapping-redwood.pdf — condensed mapping of diagram elements to SIG/CAIQ control IDs
- deployment-trace-20260708.txt — redacted request trace showing isolation enforcement points and audit log entries (timestamps redacted)

Quick summary to hand to auditors:
1) Isolation is enforced at multiple layers (compute, network, control-plane) — no single network path exists from a Dedicated tenant worker to another customer’s Dedicated worker; Private deployments use customer-managed VPC routing.
2) Control-plane operations are tenant-scoped via tokenized RPCs and RBAC; for Private deployments a private control-plane option removes cross-tenant metadata flow.
3) Egress is strictly constrained by allowlists; cross-tenant egress to public endpoints is logged and subject to automated alerting.
4) All evidence ties to SIG/CAIQ controls as annotated in the attached PDF.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute auditor walk-through where Karthik goes over the CAIQ mappings line-by-line.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference
